# Long context has several axes: position, access, and state compression

[简体中文](../../../../learning/deep-dives/foundation-models/context-and-state.md) · English

Updated 2026-11-27 · 52 topic entries / 26 representative comparisons

Ask first how history is stored and then how the current token reads it. RoPE changes relative position relationships; Mamba writes history into recurrence; NSA splits access across paths; OpenAttention retains proxies for unread content; and TTR fits an input-conditioned compression. MERLIN keeps routing-key moments beside compressed segment states to change how segments are read without replacing their internal recurrent writes. A single supported-length number cannot rank these designs.

[Mechanisms](#comparison) · [Trade-offs](#analysis) · [Cross-paper questions](#questions) · [Updates](#updates)

!!! note "How to read this card"

    The table compares representative methods. It is not a shared-benchmark leaderboard. Teaching examples are not measured results.

## Mechanism comparison {#comparison}

Axes: Token-level KV, recurrent state, or input-conditioned compression coefficients · Whether the current query can revisit exact details · Whether unread history is omitted, summarized, or already folded into state · Costs in training, forward solving, or index access

## Trade-off analysis {#analysis}

### Expressible position is not accessible history

RoPE defines how QK carries relative position, but full attention still processes visible history. Mamba changes storage and propagation, replacing per-token access with state. Position extrapolation failure and forgetting a detail in state are different; extra state alone cannot explain the former and changing positions cannot fix the latter. Identify whether the task needs exact lookup or persistent state updates.

Sources: [RoFormer: Enhanced Transformer with Rotary Position Embedding](../../../../reproductions/2104.09864-rope/README-en.md) · [Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces](../../../../reproductions/2312.00752-mamba/README-en.md)

### Can compressed history still expose details?

NSA's compressed branch sits beside query-conditioned exact block reads. OpenAttention spends budget on exact rows and leaves the rest in normalization as log-count mean proxies. TTR maps whole groups to regression coefficients with no per-item invertibility guarantee. Trace where missing information goes rather than counting output vectors. Local formulas or short runs do not rank long-text capability.

Sources: [Native Sparse Attention: Hardware-Aligned and Natively Trainable Sparse Attention](../../../../reproductions/2502.11089-native-sparse-attention/README-en.md) · [OpenAttention: One Percent Is Enough with Tail Proxies](../../../../foundation-models/2610.30951-openattention/README-en.md) · [Rethinking Sequence Compression with Test-time Regression](../../../../foundation-models/2610.31574-ttr-compressor/README-en.md)

### October 29: new methods and evidence boundaries

Select-TTT changes how strongly each context chunk writes to fast weights based on current query token probability mass; apply-before-write preserves temporal order. Clipping can leave the total below the chunk count and must not be renormalized to fake conservation. Sleep separates active learning from offline consolidation; locally only LTI reward runs. Its full method trains added parameters, so the reward operator does not establish memory written into the model.

Sources: [RoFormer: Enhanced Transformer with Rotary Position Embedding](../../../../reproductions/2104.09864-rope/README-en.md) · [Select-TTT: Query-Conditioned Selective Fast Weight Updates for In-Place Test-Time Training](../../../../foundation-models/2610.36794-select-ttt/README-en.md) · [Language Models Need Sleep: Learning to Self-Modify and Consolidate Memories](../../../../foundation-models/2606.03979-sleep-lti/README-en.md)

### Write state first, then choose which segments to read

Mamba's selective recurrence controls what enters a state; MERLIN assumes compressed segments and readouts already exist and routes the current query among them. Equal key means can hide a few strong matches. Raw second moments recover aligned variance but not missing within-segment detail. Eq. 9 normalizes means and variances separately before mixing, unlike mixing logits then softmax. Equal-length segments and causal visibility are required.

Sources: [Multi-State Linear Attention with Generalized Second-Order Routing](../../../../foundation-models/2610.37645-merlin/README-en.md) · [Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces](../../../../reproductions/2312.00752-mamba/README-en.md)

### Retaining original history and sharing compressed state are different access routes

NSA preserves distinct detail-access paths through summaries, selected blocks and sliding windows. Without retraining the model, CSB reorganizes original KV into semantic blocks and reads whole blocks. Anchor instead shares an already compressed recurrent state across layers, aligns coordinate frames with per-layer read maps, and gates the result into local output. CSB centroids select content; they do not replace the values read. Anchor still depends on a real writer: injecting a matrix externally does not implement TTT. Also separate causal support from index construction: although CSB masks future positions, whole-prompt clustering can let future keys change earlier routing, so it does not establish a strictly streaming-causal language model. Neither local L1 component provides full-model capability, end-to-end speedup or evidence for Evolve promotion.

Sources: [Native Sparse Attention: Hardware-Aligned and Natively Trainable Sparse Attention](../../../../reproductions/2502.11089-native-sparse-attention/README-en.md) · [Coarse Semantic Blocks for Efficient Training-Free Sparse Attention](../../../../foundation-models/2611.04313-semantic-block-sparse-attention/README-en.md) · [Anchor: Augmented Cross-Layer Recurrent State for Long-Context Retrieval in Test-Time Training](../../../../foundation-models/2611.04327-anchor-kv/README-en.md)

### A position-bias window is not a window on visible history

RoPE rotates Q and K so relative displacement enters their dot product. ConvPE predicts an input-dependent score adjustment from recent hidden states; visible keys outside the bias window still enter softmax with their original QK scores. CSB instead selects whole blocks of original KV and changes the support. These are changes to dot-product representation, additive scores, and support, respectively; W is not a KV budget. ConvPE also requires actual left-context hidden states for chunked decoding. Agreement between chunked and full-sequence slices verifies the bias contract, not long-context capability or speed.

Sources: [RoFormer: Enhanced Transformer with Rotary Position Embedding](../../../../reproductions/2104.09864-rope/README-en.md) · [ConvPE: Convolutional Position Embedding Improves Transformers](../../../../foundation-models/2611.07749-convpe/README-en.md) · [Coarse Semantic Blocks for Efficient Training-Free Sparse Attention](../../../../foundation-models/2611.04313-semantic-block-sparse-attention/README-en.md)

### Identify whether the saving comes from prefix scanning or approximating unread mass

ADIndex reuses candidate scanning across neighboring queries before query-specific refinement. The bank sees only anchor history; later queries add newly visible tokens. OpenAttention instead represents unread KV clusters with count-weighted mean proxies in a joint softmax with exact rows. The first does not preserve all unread probability mass, while the second does not retain exact within-cluster detail. Read percentages alone do not make them equivalent compression schemes.

Sources: [ADIndex: Layer-Adaptive Sparse Attention Indexing via Group-Level Distillation](../../../../foundation-models/2611.12956-adindex/README-en.md) · [OpenAttention: One Percent Is Enough with Tail Proxies](../../../../foundation-models/2610.30951-openattention/README-en.md)

### ECG: shared representations for retrieval and context compression: intervention and evidence are different axes

No. ECG compresses external documents into shared semantic vectors. ADIndex shares attention candidate banks, then refines per query and adds newly visible tokens. Their support, fidelity and cost units differ. Compression genuinely consumes stored E_ret. Teacher distributions/relevance are detached while alpha and temperature remain differentiable. FKL sums answer-token KLs before batch averaging; margin uses declared hard negatives only. The paper specifies a large positive gate bias but no exact value: five is an explicit local convention. There is no pretrained decoder, index, special-token integration or full training pipeline.

Sources: [A Unified Model and Document Representation for On-Device Retrieval-Augmented Generation](../../../../foundation-models/2604.14403-ecg-rag/README-en.md) · [ADIndex: Layer-Adaptive Sparse Attention Indexing via Group-Level Distillation](../../../../foundation-models/2611.12956-adindex/README-en.md)

### Sharing one representation and aligning several are different system choices

ECG-RAG jointly learns retrieval/compression to avoid duplicate storage and still needs decoder training. HVMap accepts already heterogeneous encoders, using paired maps and two-space scoring. Fuzzy diagonal terms anchor absolute correspondence; relative RKD geometry is insufficient. SCORE2 retains each native vector rather than always favoring the hub. Small-tensor gradients establish neither cross-modal retrieval nor index throughput, so author campaign results must not become local dashboard claims.

Sources: [Federated Vector Retrieval across Heterogeneous VectorDBs](../../../../foundation-models/2611.01514-hvmap/README-en.md) · [A Unified Model and Document Representation for On-Device Retrieval-Augmented Generation](../../../../foundation-models/2604.14403-ecg-rag/README-en.md)

### InfuseLoop: causal cross-trajectory latent injection

Anchor shares an external TTT state with learned read maps. InfuseLoop aggregates trajectory latents admitted by a parallel execution graph; arbitrary cross-layer averaging is not equivalent. Both keys and values use parameter-free RMS normalization. Document boundaries are masked before softmax. Every new state reads the same old buffer, with commit only after the cycle. The aggregate replaces the prior cross-loop input rather than being added twice.

Sources: [InfuseLoop: Cross-Trajectory Latent Injection for Scalable Parallel Looped Transformers](../../../../foundation-models/2611.22426-infuseloop/README-en.md) · [Anchor: Augmented Cross-Layer Recurrent State for Long-Context Retrieval in Test-Time Training](../../../../foundation-models/2611.04327-anchor-kv/README-en.md)

### Compare state dependency graphs before complexity labels

The Mamba README gives h_t=exp(Delta_t A)h_(t-1)+Delta_t B_t x_t on a one-dimensional chain and notes that its short-budget WikiText negative result does not represent paper scale. FM-Mamba cross-couples two axis steps in ZOH coefficients and retains the diagonal predecessor; cells on one anti-diagonal can run together. Its frozen-position stability condition is not a global theorem for arbitrary changing coefficient fields. Input dependence alone does not equalize their topology, discretization or parallel execution.

Sources: [FM-Mamba: An Efficient Native 2D Selective State Space Model with Stability-Aware Discretization](../../../../foundation-models/2611.22061-fm-mamba/README-en.md) · [Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces](../../../../reproductions/2312.00752-mamba/README-en.md)

### GaugeRoPE: executable rotary carriers plus residual KV codes

Anchor shares TTT state across layers with learned read maps. GaugeRoPE retains per-layer token history in low-rank compatible coordinates. Cross-layer sharing and per-token latent compression are different interventions. The retained carrier executes RoPE exactly, but RKV replaces residual position-dependent scores with an unrotated correction. Overall attention remains approximate. PCA uses explicit calibration inputs and does not choose ranks from test answers.

Sources: [GaugeRoPE: RoPE-Compatible Executable Latent Attention](../../../../foundation-models/2611.20524-gaugerope/README-en.md) · [Anchor: Augmented Cross-Layer Recurrent State for Long-Context Retrieval in Test-Time Training](../../../../foundation-models/2611.04327-anchor-kv/README-en.md)

### simq: distinguish mechanism from capability

SectionIII/Algorithms1–2 retain sampling, graph-guided assignment, deferred splitting, normalized centroids, token-wise candidates and exact MaxSim reranking. SIMQ+ in SectionV/Algorithm3 counts distinct document membership in each raw token pool without TopDocs truncation. All boundary-count ties are retained, so the pool may exceedNmin. The local Index uses exact finite kNN graph construction and bounded Lloyd splitting instead of scalable HNSW/VSAG backends; this is an explicit small-data deviation, not an industrial build/QPS reproduction. HVMap handles incompatible encoder spaces through hub mappings and native/mapped SCORE2 reranking. SIMQ assumes one normalized token space and changes graph organization and late-interaction computation. SIMQ hit counts do not validate mapping quality, and HVMap tensor losses do not establish graph efficiency.

Sources: [SIMQ: A Single Graph-based Index for Multi-Vector Query](../../../../foundation-models/2611.22079-simq/README-en.md) · [Federated Vector Retrieval across Heterogeneous VectorDBs](../../../../foundation-models/2611.01514-hvmap/README-en.md)

### unigraph: distinguish mechanism from capability

Algorithm1 takes top-kg neighbors peralpha and retainsM by occurrence frequency. Algorithm2 maintains candidate and ef-sized result sets under query-specific hybrid distance. Dense-first pruning uses a Cauchy–Schwarz norm bound to avoid some sparse inner products: gamma=1 is a safe lower bound, while gamma<1 is a more aggressive estimate without that guarantee. Main experiments usegamma=0.3; local controls usegamma=1 against unpruned beam results. The guide is dense abovealpha0.5 and sparse otherwise;0.5 is the paper’s comparable-scale convention. HVMap learns representation mappings across heterogeneous databases. UniGraph does not learn a new mapping; it retains dense/sparse components and changes neighborhoods across weights. SCORE2 native/mapped weights and UniGraph semantic/lexical alpha have different meanings and are not interchangeable.

Sources: [UniGraph: A Unified Graph-based Index for Dynamic Hybrid Dense-Sparse Vector Retrieval](../../../../foundation-models/2611.20758-unigraph/README-en.md) · [Federated Vector Retrieval across Heterogeneous VectorDBs](../../../../foundation-models/2611.01514-hvmap/README-en.md)

### dealrank: distinguish mechanism from capability

For100 candidates, Section2.1 uses five hands of20, keeps four per hand and reranks the final20: six calls in two rounds. A consistent ranker guarantees only topq=4 recovery, not top10. The500 schedule is25 hands keeping three then four keeping five; the1,000 schedule is50 keeping two then five keeping four, both three rounds. Later eliminations precede earlier ones. Real ThreadPool calls must return an exact permutation of their input IDs; this tests schedules, not LLM ranking quality. HVMap changes cross-space candidate mapping/scoring. DealRank does not train representations; it schedules existing candidates into ranker calls. They can compose in a retrieval pipeline, but fewer calls do not establish better alignment, and correct SCORE2 does not prove lossless listwise quotas.

Sources: [Deal With It: On Better Schedules for Listwise Reranking](../../../../foundation-models/2611.22392-dealrank/README-en.md) · [Federated Vector Retrieval across Heterogeneous VectorDBs](../../../../foundation-models/2611.01514-hvmap/README-en.md)

### Kernel Ridge Attention: Nonlinear Memory with Selective Forgetting

Mamba controls an SSM with input-dependent steps and read/write vectors. KRA additionally maintains covariance to handle correlated-key interference, costing D-squared state per head. Bounded context-independent state does not make their costs identical. Keys and queries share unit-norm sine/cosine features. P rotates and rescales a write; it is not a scalar gate. An independent dual reference solves each causal prefix with the product of content and OU-time Gram matrices.

Sources: [Kernel Ridge Attention: Nonlinear Memory with Selective Forgetting](../../../../foundation-models/2611.23896-kernel-ridge-attention/README-en.md) · [Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces](../../../../reproductions/2312.00752-mamba/README-en.md)

### HiSA: Sparsifying the Hidden Dimension of RoPE Attention in LLMs

RoFormer keeps every RoPE pair and encodes relative position by rotation. HiSA additionally removes pair contributions according to distance and frequency. This changes scoring and does not prove that switching an existing checkpoint without training preserves quality. Whole-token eviction cannot express retaining only a key's slow-frequency pairs. The rule compares the unwrapped relative angle strictly with Phi, not its remainder modulo2pi. Scaling stays1/sqrt(d), not the number of surviving dimensions. A key with no active pair must leave softmax; a zero logit would still attract probability. Future keys are masked. Infinite Phi recovers dense RoPE. Local positions are nonnegative signed-int64-range integers. uint64 bounds are checked before casting; other integers are converted before subtraction. Differences between nonnegative int64 values cannot overflow, and uint8 wraparound must not expose future keys.

Sources: [HiSA: Sparsifying the Hidden Dimension of RoPE Attention in LLMs](../../../../foundation-models/2611.26363-hisa/README-en.md) · [RoFormer: Enhanced Transformer with Rotary Position Embedding](../../../../reproductions/2104.09864-rope/README-en.md)

### Physics of Language Models: Part 4.2, Canon Layers at Scale where Synthetic Pretraining Resonates in Reality

Canon's causal width4 residual supplies local token mixing, not a long-history state or independent access to arbitrary distant positions; it can augment attention, linear attention or SSMs. Mamba also maintains input-selective recurrent state beyond its local convolution. These roles differ. Align parameters/state and tuning, then separately test retrieval: stronger knowledge scores do not establish attention-like remote reads from fixed-size state. Canon is a per-channel causal width4 convolution with left zero padding and a hidden-state residual. A/C follow normalization, B follows QKV projections, and D covers both gated-MLP branches. The rank constraint applies before SiLU; the activated gate need not be low-rank. Released LlamaCanon also uses quarter RoPE, so its differences are not solely convolution.

Sources: [Physics of Language Models: Part 4.2, Canon Layers at Scale where Synthetic Pretraining Resonates in Reality](../../../../foundation-models/2611.24963-canon-layers-scale/README-en.md) · [Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces](../../../../reproductions/2312.00752-mamba/README-en.md)

### Eliciting the Recall Capacity of Linear Attention

MERLIN changes multi-state readout using routing-key first/second moments; TLCE changes supervision allocation. Flexible readout does not establish learned recall, while weighting cannot recover information absent from state. Joint benefits require matched model/data budgets and are not established by existing small components. Short windows contain at most512tokens, reset state/attention, and run without gradients; weights are also detached. Full-training combined experiments include sentence repetition, absent locally. The loss interface is not a reproduction of the paper's recall comparison.

Sources: [Eliciting the Recall Capacity of Linear Attention](../../../../foundation-models/2611.32969-thresholded-longce/README-en.md) · [Multi-State Linear Attention with Generalized Second-Order Routing](../../../../foundation-models/2610.37645-merlin/README-en.md)

### RAP: Radial-Angular Random Projection for Hyperbolic Representations

HVMap learns paired mappings between heterogeneous encoder spaces and combines native/mapped scores. RAP does not align encoders or permit mixing arbitrary curvatures or origins. Their L1 components do not establish comparative semantic retrieval gains. These are Eq.11–12. Reject a non-origin direction in the projection kernel; map the origin to the target origin. Same-ray distances are exact, but arbitrary pairwise distances are not lossless.

Sources: [RAP: Radial-Angular Random Projection for Hyperbolic Representations](../../../../foundation-models/2611.34298-rap/README-en.md) · [Federated Vector Retrieval across Heterogeneous VectorDBs](../../../../foundation-models/2611.01514-hvmap/README-en.md)

### Integral DeltaNet: Improved Linear Attention with Adaptive Memory Integration

KRA maintains regression coefficients and posterior covariance, restoring writable uncertainty under forgetting. Integral instead stores a delta state and its weighted history. Covariance is not a memory copy, and integral history does not implement KRA covariance-guided interference correction. Local L1 cannot compare language recall. The first equation is GDN-2; broadcasting one beta across erase/write gives KDA. Lambda and gamma act on key channels, not value rows or one scalar. Integrate the updated S. The paper uses rank128 gates initialized near lambda=1-gamma=1/1024; the local rank is reduced but the trainable parameterization is retained.

Sources: [Integral DeltaNet: Improved Linear Attention with Adaptive Memory Integration](../../../../foundation-models/2611.32063-integral-deltanet/README-en.md) · [Kernel Ridge Attention: Nonlinear Memory with Selective Forgetting](../../../../foundation-models/2611.23896-kernel-ridge-attention/README-en.md)

## Cross-paper questions {#questions}

Try answering before expanding the explanation. Each question relates at least two papers.

### Why are changing RoPE and switching to recurrence not the same fix for a forgotten early one-off identifier? {#cross-position-versus-memory}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** RoPE changes position in QK, not access to original evidence. Mamba changes selective state writing; if it omits the identifier, no original KV remains to query. Diagnose position distortion, invisibility, or compression loss first, then decide whether to use detail access such as NSA.

    **Illustrative example:** An order ID appears once on the contract cover. Correct relative positions do not ensure it is read, and bounded state does not retain every ID.

    Sources: [RoFormer: Enhanced Transformer with Rotary Position Embedding](../../../../reproductions/2104.09864-rope/README-en.md) · [Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces](../../../../reproductions/2312.00752-mamba/README-en.md) · [Native Sparse Attention: Hardware-Aligned and Natively Trainable Sparse Attention](../../../../reproductions/2502.11089-native-sparse-attention/README-en.md)

### How do selected NSA blocks and OpenAttention unread-cluster proxies handle omissions differently? {#cross-tail-proxy-versus-selection}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** NSA gates overview, selected blocks, and recent-window outputs; OpenAttention includes unread clusters as count-corrected proxies in the same attention normalization as exact rows. Multiple coverage paths and tail mass/value approximation can both lose within-group details.

    **Illustrative example:** One outlier among 100 records can be diluted by either a coarse summary or a mean; test whether selection routes it to an exact read.

    Sources: [Native Sparse Attention: Hardware-Aligned and Natively Trainable Sparse Attention](../../../../reproductions/2502.11089-native-sparse-attention/README-en.md) · [OpenAttention: One Percent Is Enough with Tail Proxies](../../../../foundation-models/2610.30951-openattention/README-en.md)

### Do TTR input-wise fitting and Mamba per-token state updates mean the deployment model trains its weights? {#cross-input-adaptation-versus-parameter-update}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. TTR solves coefficients in the current group's forward pass using outer-trained targets and regularization. Mamba uses fixed parameters and current tokens to update state. These are input-dependent computation or runtime state, not optimizer updates, and have different solve versus recurrence costs.

    **Illustrative example:** One frozen model can produce different states and coefficients for two texts without writing a new checkpoint.

    Sources: [Rethinking Sequence Compression with Test-time Regression](../../../../foundation-models/2610.31574-ttr-compressor/README-en.md) · [Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces](../../../../reproductions/2312.00752-mamba/README-en.md)

### What actual execution is evidenced by query-conditioned write coefficients versus Sleep reward changes? {#cross-oct29-method-boundary}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Local Select-TTT updates a small fast-weight matrix, allowing pre-write outputs and final state checks. Local Sleep returns a reward without an optimizer or parameter expansion. Neither establishes long-context capability, and reward is not long-term retention.

    **Illustrative example:** Updating a memory table and scoring a continuation 0.9 are different evidence.

    Sources: [RoFormer: Enhanced Transformer with Rotary Position Embedding](../../../../reproductions/2104.09864-rope/README-en.md) · [Select-TTT: Query-Conditioned Selective Fast Weight Updates for In-Place Test-Time Training](../../../../foundation-models/2610.36794-select-ttt/README-en.md) · [Language Models Need Sleep: Learning to Self-Modify and Consolidate Memories](../../../../foundation-models/2606.03979-sleep-lti/README-en.md)

### Does adding a second moment turn MERLIN's bounded Mamba-like state into full attention? {#cross-merlin-routing-not-state-recurrence}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. The moment estimates alignment variance between the query and each segment's routing keys to combine readouts. Token values remain compressed and are not individually normalized; an added access cue cannot reverse compression.

    **Illustrative example:** Means of 1 do not distinguish a segment of all ones from a segment of −1 and 3. Variance distinguishes them but cannot reconstruct every original record.

    Sources: [Multi-State Linear Attention with Generalized Second-Order Routing](../../../../foundation-models/2610.37645-merlin/README-en.md) · [Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces](../../../../reproductions/2312.00752-mamba/README-en.md)

### If CSB selects history positions and Anchor shares a state, why can't a causal mask alone establish their full long-context capability? {#cross-nov04b-routing-versus-shared-state}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** CSB masks future positions in original-QKV attention, but whole-prompt clustering can let future keys influence centroids and earlier selections; masking does not remove that indexing dependency. Anchor's read maps and gates specify how to read external shared state, while correct memory content still depends on the actual TTT writer and training. Local L1 contracts separately verify selection/attention and shared readout. They establish neither strict streaming-causal invariance nor long-range retrieval capability.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: Appending new keys and rebuilding clusters may change earlier block selections. Likewise, a correct Anchor reader output from a manually supplied matrix does not show that a model learned to write an order number into it.

    Sources: [Coarse Semantic Blocks for Efficient Training-Free Sparse Attention](../../../../foundation-models/2611.04313-semantic-block-sparse-attention/README-en.md) · [Anchor: Augmented Cross-Layer Recurrent State for Long-Context Retrieval in Test-Time Training](../../../../foundation-models/2611.04327-anchor-kv/README-en.md)

### With ConvPE bias window W = 4, does a causally visible key at lag 8 disappear? What does CSB do differently? {#cross-nov06-bias-window-not-support}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. ConvPE adds zero bias, preserving the original QK score and causal mask. In CSB, if the block containing that key is not selected and the key is outside the always-visible region, it is excluded from attention support. In ConvPE, W = 4 also means that the first query in a chunk needs at most three earlier raw hidden states, not that it can see only four historical positions.

    **Illustrative example:** Example: A lag-8 key with a high original score can still receive high weight after ConvPE adds zero. If CSB excludes it, its original value cannot contribute to that query's readout.

    Sources: [ConvPE: Convolutional Position Embedding Improves Transformers](../../../../foundation-models/2611.07749-convpe/README-en.md) · [Coarse Semantic Blocks for Efficient Training-Free Sparse Attention](../../../../foundation-models/2611.04313-semantic-block-sparse-attention/README-en.md)

### Do an ADIndex shared bank and OpenAttention tail proxies have the same missed-read semantics? {#cross-shared-bank-versus-tail-proxy}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. ADIndex shares candidate search and still chooses a query-specific final Top-K; positions outside the candidate union receive no automatic proxy mass. OpenAttention keeps counted proxies for unread clusters, but their content is approximate and must exclude already read rows. Check index coverage and residual softmax mass separately.

    **Illustrative example:** A position outside ADIndex's candidate union cannot enter that refinement. In OpenAttention, it may still contribute through a residual cluster mean and count, without retaining all its individual detail.

    Sources: [ADIndex: Layer-Adaptive Sparse Attention Indexing via Group-Level Distillation](../../../../foundation-models/2611.12956-adindex/README-en.md) · [OpenAttention: One Percent Is Enough with Tail Proxies](../../../../foundation-models/2610.30951-openattention/README-en.md)

### Is ECG equivalent to ADIndex sparse retrieval? {#cross-nov13-colm-ecg-rag}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. ECG compresses external documents into shared semantic vectors. ADIndex shares attention candidate banks, then refines per query and adds newly visible tokens. Their support, fidelity and cost units differ.

    **Illustrative example:** Eliminating duplicate document vectors is not the same as avoiding scans of historical attention keys.

    Sources: [A Unified Model and Document Representation for On-Device Retrieval-Augmented Generation](../../../../foundation-models/2604.14403-ecg-rag/README-en.md) · [ADIndex: Layer-Adaptive Sparse Attention Indexing via Group-Level Distillation](../../../../foundation-models/2611.12956-adindex/README-en.md)

### Do ECG shared representations plus a low HVMap fuzzy loss prove better RAG? {#cross-cross-nov18-hvmap-alignment}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. They change different stages, and local components lack complete training, retrieval and answer evaluation. HVMap needs semantic generalization and union rankings; ECG needs compressed-context generation. Diagnostic loss is not end-to-end capability.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: successful backpropagation does not put a relevant document in top ten or make an answer correct.

    Sources: [Federated Vector Retrieval across Heterogeneous VectorDBs](../../../../foundation-models/2611.01514-hvmap/README-en.md) · [A Unified Model and Document Representation for On-Device Retrieval-Augmented Generation](../../../../foundation-models/2604.14403-ecg-rag/README-en.md)

### How does this differ from Anchor? {#cross-nov18-infuseloop}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Anchor reads external TTT memory alongside local attention. InfuseLoop aggregates trajectory hidden states according to cycle availability.

    **Illustrative example:** Broadcasting one KV matrix across loops does not implement cross-trajectory indexing.

    Sources: [InfuseLoop: Cross-Trajectory Latent Injection for Scalable Parallel Looped Transformers](../../../../foundation-models/2611.22426-infuseloop/README-en.md) · [Anchor: Augmented Cross-Layer Recurrent State for Long-Context Retrieval in Test-Time Training](../../../../foundation-models/2611.04327-anchor-kv/README-en.md)

### Why is flattened-image Mamba not FM-Mamba? {#cross-nov18-fm-mamba}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** It changes the dependency graph. Native FM-Mamba reads upper, left and diagonal predecessors using two axis steps and stability projection; a flattened scan follows one chosen chain.

    **Illustrative example:** An upper-left impulse can reach the next diagonal cell through an explicit predecessor term; removing that term changes the recurrence.

    Sources: [FM-Mamba: An Efficient Native 2D Selective State Space Model with Stability-Aware Discretization](../../../../foundation-models/2611.22061-fm-mamba/README-en.md) · [Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces](../../../../reproductions/2312.00752-mamba/README-en.md)

### How does it differ from Anchor state sharing? {#cross-nov18-gaugerope}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** It reduces per-token, per-layer dimensions with frequency structure. Anchor shares recurrent state across layers and needs writer/read-map semantics.

    **Illustrative example:** Equal byte savings do not imply equal information or update behavior.

    Sources: [GaugeRoPE: RoPE-Compatible Executable Latent Attention](../../../../foundation-models/2611.20524-gaugerope/README-en.md) · [Anchor: Augmented Cross-Layer Recurrent State for Long-Context Retrieval in Test-Time Training](../../../../foundation-models/2611.04327-anchor-kv/README-en.md)

### Can SIMQ replace HVMap heterogeneous-space alignment? {#cross-cross-nov18-latest-simq}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. SIMQ changes candidate indexing within one token space; HVMap learns cross-space mappings.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: equal vector dimensionality does not make two encoders comparable by SIMQ inner products.

    Sources: [SIMQ: A Single Graph-based Index for Multi-Vector Query](../../../../foundation-models/2611.22079-simq/README-en.md) · [Federated Vector Retrieval across Heterogeneous VectorDBs](../../../../foundation-models/2611.01514-hvmap/README-en.md)

### Is UniGraph alpha the HVMap native weight? {#cross-cross-nov18-latest-unigraph}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. It mixes dense/sparse distances, whereas HVMap weights native/mapped scores.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: raisingalpha does not mean trusting a candidate’s own database more.

    Sources: [UniGraph: A Unified Graph-based Index for Dynamic Hybrid Dense-Sparse Vector Retrieval](../../../../foundation-models/2611.20758-unigraph/README-en.md) · [Federated Vector Retrieval across Heterogeneous VectorDBs](../../../../foundation-models/2611.01514-hvmap/README-en.md)

### Can it replace HVMap dual-space reranking? {#cross-cross-nov18-latest-dealrank}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. DealRank determines which candidates share a comparison; HVMap defines comparable cross-encoder scores.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: dealing cannot align incompatible embeddings.

    Sources: [Deal With It: On Better Schedules for Listwise Reranking](../../../../foundation-models/2611.22392-dealrank/README-en.md) · [Federated Vector Retrieval across Heterogeneous VectorDBs](../../../../foundation-models/2611.01514-hvmap/README-en.md)

### What extra state distinguishes it from Mamba? {#cross-nov19-kernel-ridge-attention}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** KRA stores a per-head D-by-D covariance in addition to regression coefficients. Mamba selective scans do not maintain that posterior geometry.

    **Illustrative example:** Doubling D quadruples covariance elements even with fixed context length.

    Sources: [Kernel Ridge Attention: Nonlinear Memory with Selective Forgetting](../../../../foundation-models/2611.23896-kernel-ridge-attention/README-en.md) · [Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces](../../../../reproductions/2312.00752-mamba/README-en.md)

### How does this differ from RoFormer plus a token window? {#cross-nov20-hisa}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** RoFormer uses all pairs. A token window drops whole keys; HiSA gives frequency pairs distinct distance windows while keeping the original1/sqrt(d) scale.

    **Illustrative example:** With d64 and only16 surviving components, divide by8, not4.

    Sources: [HiSA: Sparsifying the Hidden Dimension of RoPE Attention in LLMs](../../../../foundation-models/2611.26363-hisa/README-en.md) · [RoFormer: Enhanced Transformer with Rotary Position Embedding](../../../../reproductions/2104.09864-rope/README-en.md)

### Is a30% token saving a30% training speedup? {#cross-nov20-canon-layers-scale}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. Per-step cost and the target skill must also match. With the paper's illustrative13% naive step overhead,0.7 times1.13 is about0.79, or roughly21% less time.

    **Illustrative example:** Using30% fewer tokens with13% slower steps does not take70% of the original time.

    Sources: [Physics of Language Models: Part 4.2, Canon Layers at Scale where Synthetic Pretraining Resonates in Reality](../../../../foundation-models/2611.24963-canon-layers-scale/README-en.md) · [Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces](../../../../reproductions/2312.00752-mamba/README-en.md)

### Can TLCE replace MERLIN's multi-state routing? {#cross-nov25-thresholded-longce}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. TLCE reallocates loss without changing memory structure; MERLIN changes segment-state readout. Missing information and unlearned use of available information are different bottlenecks.

    **Illustrative example:** Illustration: weighting a later token cannot guarantee recovery after two histories become indistinguishable in one state; preserving multiple states changes what can be read.

    Sources: [Eliciting the Recall Capacity of Linear Attention](../../../../foundation-models/2611.32969-thresholded-longce/README-en.md) · [Multi-State Linear Attention with Generalized Second-Order Routing](../../../../foundation-models/2610.37645-merlin/README-en.md)

### Can RAP replace HVMap for cross-encoder alignment? {#cross-nov26-rap}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. RAP compresses one defined hyperbolic space; HVMap learns paired mappings between heterogeneous spaces. Radial preservation provides no semantic correspondence.

    **Illustrative example:** Illustration:if two encoders place an object in different directions, preserving their radii does not align those directions.

    Sources: [RAP: Radial-Angular Random Projection for Hyperbolic Representations](../../../../foundation-models/2611.34298-rap/README-en.md) · [Federated Vector Retrieval across Heterogeneous VectorDBs](../../../../foundation-models/2611.01514-hvmap/README-en.md)

### Why is KRA covariance P not an integral state? {#cross-nov27-integral-deltanet}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** P represents uncertainty and changes writes; X stores weighted S history and only participates in readout. Their semantics and updates differ.

    **Illustrative example:** Illustration:KRA forgetting can restore P without a new value,whereas X remains retained S history,not a write-gain matrix.

    Sources: [Integral DeltaNet: Improved Linear Attention with Adaptive Memory Integration](../../../../foundation-models/2611.32063-integral-deltanet/README-en.md) · [Kernel Ridge Attention: Nonlinear Memory with Selective Forgetting](../../../../foundation-models/2611.23896-kernel-ridge-attention/README-en.md)
